faq.title: AJV6D Sportbrake FAQs
faq.description: Answers to common questions about costs, codes, warranty and fitting for the Jaguar XF Sportbrake AJV6D engine.

faqs.q: Are the AJV6D and 306DT the same engine?
faqs.a: They describe the same 3.0 V6 diesel family. AJV6D is the engineering name, while 306DT is the parts code. Variants still differ, so we confirm your exact engine using the VIN.

faqs.q: How much does a Jaguar XF Sportbrake AJV6D engine replacement cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the engine type you choose and whether we install it. Send your registration and we'll provide an itemised written quote covering parts and labour.

faqs.q: Is a warranty included with your AJV6D engines?
faqs.a: Yes. Every engine we supply comes with a six-month mechanical warranty. We'll explain the cover and any conditions, including those for outside fitting, before you place an order.

faqs.q: Was the 2012 XF Sportbrake available with a 211hp V6?
faqs.a: Sportbrake data for 2012 to 2015 lists the V6 diesel at 240hp and 275hp. The 211hp tune appears in XF saloon listings, so we always verify output using your VIN.

faqs.q: What are typical Jaguar XF Sportbrake AJV6D engine problems?
faqs.a: Reported issues include crankshaft bearing wear, crank pulley failure, turbo actuator faults and oil cooler leaks. Several symptoms overlap, so a proper diagnosis should come before any repair decision.

faqs.q: Can you send an AJV6D to my local garage?
faqs.a: Yes. Supply-only engines are delivered by pallet across the UK, to your address or a chosen garage. We confirm compatibility first and explain warranty conditions for third-party fitting.

faqs.q: What happens during your supply and fit service?
faqs.a: At our Grays, Essex workshop we remove the failed V6, install the replacement, refill fluids, complete any software setup and road test the car. Timescales are confirmed with your quote.

workshopIntro.title: Making a Sound Decision About Your AJV6D
workshopIntro.description: Diagnose before you decide. Crank pulley failures, turbo actuator faults and oil cooler leaks are often repairable without replacing the engine. If bearing failure has damaged the crankshaft or block, compare the repair figure against your Sportbrake's mileage, condition and value.
paragraphs: Your Jaguar XF Sportbrake AJV6D engine replacement cost will reflect the engine type, its history and whether we fit it. Labour on a V6 diesel is significant, so a complete supply and fit quote gives a more realistic comparison than an engine-only price.

When reviewing AJV6D 3.0 V6 diesel engine UK listings, confirm the donor vehicle, output and recorded mileage. Engines from other models may need different parts, so detailed answers help protect you from costly surprises later.

Lastly, look closely at warranty terms. A Jaguar XF Sportbrake AJV6D engine with warranty gives protection should a mechanical fault arise after fitting. Engines we supply carry a six-month mechanical warranty, and we explain the conditions before you order.

engineProblems.title: Jaguar XF Sportbrake AJV6D Engine Problems and Signs
engineProblems.description: These warning signs may point to a fault that diagnosis must confirm.

cards.title: Bottom-End Knock
cards.description: A knock from low in the engine that grows with revs may indicate crankshaft bearing wear, reported on this V6.
cards.action: Switch off and arrange recovery immediately.

cards.title: Mid-Range Power Drop
cards.description: Strong pull that suddenly flattens might suggest the secondary turbo, its actuator or vacuum control is not working correctly.

cards.title: Oil Pressure Messages
cards.description: Intermittent oil pressure warnings could relate to low oil, a sensor fault or internal wear needing immediate investigation.
cards.action: Check the oil level before restarting.

cards.title: Crank Pulley Vibration
cards.description: Vibration at idle or a wobbling front pulley may indicate a failing crankshaft damper, which can damage the auxiliary drive.
cards.action: Book an auxiliary belt drive inspection.

cards.title: Oil or Coolant Seepage
cards.description: Fluid gathering in the engine valley or under the car could come from a leaking oil cooler or coolant pipe.
cards.action: Get the leak located and assessed.

cards.title: Smoke Under Acceleration
cards.description: Dark smoke or hesitation when accelerating may relate to EGR, injector or air intake faults rather than engine damage.
cards.action: Request an EGR and injector check.

engineOverview.title: What the AJV6D Name Means for Sportbrake Owners
paragraphs: AJV6D is the engineering name for Jaguar Land Rover's 3.0-litre V6 diesel, also called the TDV6 or SDV6. In parts catalogues the same engine is usually coded 306DT, so both labels can describe your Sportbrake's unit. It displaces 2,993cc and uses common-rail injection with twin turbochargers.

Searches for a Jaguar XF Sportbrake AJV6D engine 2012 match the first-generation estate, which was listed with 240hp and 275hp outputs. A Jaguar XF Sportbrake 3.0 V6 diesel engine 211hp listing needs checking, because the 155kW tune appears in XF saloon data rather than Sportbrake specifications.

The later X260 Sportbrake carried a 300hp development of the V6 from 2017, where electronics and ancillaries can differ. That's why we never rely on the engine name alone. Your VIN, engine number and output decide which replacement will drop in correctly.
